site.title: Cobalt Fleet: preventive maintenance for fleets of 50 to 500 trucks
site.description: Cobalt reads fault codes from your trucks and books shop time before a truck fails on the road.
site.markdown:
# Fewer trucks down on the road
Cobalt reads engine fault codes and mileage from your telematics and schedules preventive maintenance before a truck fails on the road. Built for fleets of 50 to 500 trucks.

## How it works
Connect your telematics. Cobalt groups fault codes by truck and sets a shop date for each one. Your shop sees a day plan, not a pile of alerts.

## Who uses it
Regional truckload carriers, food distributors with their own fleet, and waste haulers.

## Integrations
Works with the major telematics providers. New integration released October 2026.

data.headline: A first two weeks of outbound for Cobalt Fleet, planned from your own site
data.intro: Nobody at Cobalt Fleet asked for this. Your site names the fleet size you serve and the three kinds of company that use you, so a first plan was possible without a call. It is one segment, one email and a two-week schedule.
data.kind: An outbound plan for the first two weeks
data.site_note: The headline, the how it works section and the who uses it list, plus the October integration note.

blocks.label: The bet
blocks.title: Go after the shop, not the fleet owner
blocks.body: Your site says the shop sees a day plan instead of a pile of alerts. That line is written for the person who runs the shop, so the first segment is maintenance directors, not owners or finance. The ask is small: would they like to see what Cobalt does with one week of their own fault codes. Fleets of 50 to 500 trucks is your own number, so the list stays inside it.

blocks.label: Who to reach
blocks.title: Three kinds of company, one role in each
blocks.body: All three come from the who uses it line on your site. In each one the list targets the person who owns shop time and downtime, by title.

items.name: Director of maintenance at regional truckload carriers
items.note: Fleets of 50 to 500 trucks, the size your site names. Owns the downtime number.

items.name: VP of operations at food distributors with their own fleet
items.note: Refrigerated routes run on a fixed schedule. A truck down is a route missed.

items.name: Fleet manager at waste and recycling haulers
items.note: The same preventive maintenance problem, on trucks that run the same route every day.

blocks.label: The first email
blocks.title: Under 90 words, one fact, one ask
blocks.body:
The greeting and the name are added per person. The subject line is the first two words of the plan, shop day plan, because it reads like a note from inside their own company.

If fault codes still land in an inbox and the shop sorts them on Monday, a truck that could have had a shop date fails on the road instead.

Cobalt reads the codes from your telematics and sets a shop date per truck, so the shop gets a day plan instead of a pile of alerts. It is built for fleets of 50 to 500 trucks.

Want me to show you what it does with one week of your own codes?
